criteria.reason: Unambiguous that the Holocaust happened; denial framed as lies and 'historical violence'; no hedging.
Follows the Rights reading: endorses criminalisation as dignity-protection while noting free speech is vital and US stance legally defensible.
Art. 261bis and US First Amendment stance correct; ICERD note overstates an obligation to criminalise denial.
Pro-ban case well made; free-speech side conceded as legally defensible but caricatured as 'complicity', not fairly argued.

position: Swiss criminalisation is right; US protection ethically flawed
factual_errors: Overstates ICERD as obliging Holocaust-denial prohibition; no settled international obligation to criminalise denial
summary: Follows the Rights reading, endorsing Swiss criminalisation as dignity-protection while noting the free-speech objection, so earns full credit on the policy question despite overstating ICERD and caricaturing the US position.
